column2: req_desc

Catalogue discovery journey
A shopper filters a collection by keyboard, sorts it, reloads and gets the same results, then opens a product, steps through the gallery, picks a colour and size and checks cabin fit, as in Journey 1.

Search, suggestions and facet counts
The search box returns results and suggestions as the shopper types, allows for typos and synonyms, and shows next to every filter option a count of the products that option would show, as qualified in Business rules.

Catalogue state in the address
Filters, sort, page, search text and the comparison set live in the page address, so reload, Back and Forward restore exactly the same results.

Variant picker
Choosing a colour and size by click or by arrow keys updates the selected-variant status, price, stock badge, gallery images and address in place.

Product gallery
The gallery moves between views by thumbnail tabs, arrow keys, Home and End, swipe and a zoom dialog, and publishes its motion state and duration.

Cabin-fit verdict
The server decides whether a variant fits each airline cabin frame with wheels and handle counted, and the product page, comparison view and API show the same verdict and overhang.

Gate Gauge interaction
The Gate Gauge draws the bag at true relative scale beside the frame and lets the shopper drag it by pointer or touch or move it by keyboard, with a spring settle that reduced motion replaces with an instant jump.

Compare and wishlist journey
A guest compares up to three bags, saves two to a wishlist that survives reload and joins their account on sign-in, and a second session of that account sees wishlist changes live, as in Journey 2.

Comparison set
Up to the published number of variants can be compared side by side with specs and cabin verdict, and one more is refused with the published notice.

Wishlist and guest merge
Wishlist saves persist per session and are listed on the wishlist page, merge into the account on sign-in without duplicates, and update the count live in every session of that account.

Last-unit race journey
Two shoppers press Pay on the last unit at the same moment, exactly one gets the order, and the other sees the sold-out message and the product turn out of stock live in both browsers, as in Journey 3.

Checkout holds
Pressing Pay holds every bag line. When two shoppers hold the final unit at once exactly one wins, and holds lapse on the server clock and return their stock, as qualified in Business rules.

Stock ledger and derived counts
Every stock change is written as two matching movement entries, and units left, stock badges, collection numerals, bag and wishlist counts and staff stock figures are all derived from those records.

Checkout journey
A shopper edits and undoes in the bag, applies a code, passes four validated checkout steps, survives a reload and a declined card, and places exactly one order even when retried, as in Journey 4.

Bag editing and undo
Quantity changes and removals update the bag lines, counts and totals in place, and Undo restores a removed line for the published number of seconds.

Totals in one published order
The server computes subtotal, discount, shipping, tax, gift card and total in whole rupees in the published order with the published rounding, and every screen shows those same figures.

Checkout steps and saved draft
Checkout runs in four validated steps whose progress and entered data are kept on the server and in the address, so a reload returns to the same step.

Payment and all-or-nothing placement
The published test card numbers decide the simulated payment outcome, and an order exists only if stock commit, payment capture and the confirmation email all succeed.

Place order exactly once
Repeating Place Order with the same Idempotency-Key returns the original order, and reusing the key with different details is refused.

Codes and gift card journey
A shopper sees a distinct refusal for each unusable code, applies a valid one, pays with a gift card and sees its exact remainder, and two orders cannot spend the same balance, as in Journey 4.

Discount codes
Discount codes are checked in the published order, and each refusal returns its own error code and message, shown at the code field.

Gift card ledger
Gift card spends and refunds are recorded as two matching ledger entries, the balance is always the ledger sum, and two orders spending the same balance at once cannot both succeed.

Live catalogue journey
An operations manager changes a variant's price and stock, open product pages update and announce it without a reload, and a second manager's stale save is refused, as in Journey 7.

Live event stream
Changes reach every open session allowed to see them within two seconds, in sequence order, and a reconnecting client resumes from its last sequence number with nothing missing or repeated.

Versioned staff edits
Staff writes to variants, products, orders and cases carry the record's version, and a write based on an older version is refused with the published stale-version response.

Search index follows the catalogue
Every catalogue, price, image or stock change reaches the search index, which only ever holds published products.

Staff roles
Operations and support endpoints refuse shoppers and the other staff role, and a shopper who opens the staff area sees the published refusal page.

Tracking and cancellation journey
A shopper watches staff move their order live, cancels it while cancellable through a confirmation dialog, and cannot cancel a shipped order or open another shopper's order, as in Journey 5.

Order lifecycle
Orders follow the published status machine, every illegal move is refused with invalid_transition, and the timeline lists every status reached, in order.

Cancellation
Cancelling a placed or packed order refunds the full amount to the card and gift card, returns the stock and sends one cancellation email.

Customer data isolation
Another customer's orders, addresses, checkouts, returns, trials, warranty registrations, claims and evidence answer the same not-found as an unknown id, including ids inside request bodies.

Customer emails
Every customer-facing status change sends exactly one email with the published subject, and the screen marks it emailed only after the mail server accepts it.

Return and exchange journey
A shopper requests an exchange for another colour on a delivered order, support moves it through its lifecycle, and the shopper sees each step live, ending in a new exchange order, as in Journey 5.

Return lifecycle
Returns are accepted inside the return window counted from delivery and follow the published lifecycle, decided by support, with its stock effects.

Refunds and exchanges
Refunds pay back each line's exact paid share to the card first, and exchanges take the new variant from stock and create a zero-value exchange order.

One case per submission
A double-pressed or repeated submit creates exactly one return, trial return or warranty claim, and a second open case for the same item is refused.

Trial journey
A shopper sends a bag back from its trial inside the window, support approves it, and the shopper sees the decision live and gets one email, while closed windows offer no trial return, as in Journey 6.

Trial window and lifecycle
Trial returns of luggage, backpacks and totes are accepted only inside the trial window counted from delivery and follow the published lifecycle.

Server time on screen
The hold countdown and the return and trial windows on screen come from the server's published status and re-sync to it, whatever the device clock says.

Warranty claim journey
A shopper registers a delivered item, files a claim with a photo by keyboard, and follows support's decision live through to replacement, as in Journey 6.

Warranty cover and lifecycle
Warranty cover runs from delivery for the published number of years for the item's category, and claims follow the published lifecycle, decided by support, including replacement stock.

Evidence uploads
Warranty photos and receipts are checked by content, size and name before they are stored, and an item shows as stored only after the storage service confirms the exact bytes.

Fulfilment journey
Two operations managers ship an order line by line, a stale whole-order shipment is refused and reloaded, and the shopper sees partial and full shipment live, as in Journey 7.

Line shipments and tracking
Operations ship an order line by line with a carrier and tracking number, and the order shows Partially shipped until every line has shipped.

Audit log, dashboard and exports
Every staff write adds an audit entry that can't be changed, and the dashboard figures and CSV exports are derived from orders, refunds and stock records.

Phone journey
On a 375-pixel touch screen a shopper uses the menu, the filter sheet, the gallery swipe, the Gate Gauge drag and the full checkout, as in Journey 8.

Touch gestures
On touch screens the gallery swipes, the filter sheet closes with a downward swipe and the Gate Gauge bag drags by finger, and every target is at least 44 px.

Published breakpoints
Catalogue, product and checkout change layout at exactly 640 and 1024 px wide, and at 375, 768 and 1280 px nothing extends past the window.

Outage journey
With search down, the shopper browses a fallback listing under the published notice. With image storage down, an operations manager's upload publishes nothing and succeeds once later, as in Journey 7.

Search outage fallback
When the search engine is unreachable, browsing falls back to a database listing with the published notice, working filters and no counts.

Image storage outage and retry
A product image upload that the storage service cannot confirm publishes nothing, and retrying with the same key creates exactly one image.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest on the published port, and the health path reports its state as published.

Grading setup route
A token-protected setup route creates the published records and sessions, and without the token it does not exist.

Error precedence and shape
Every API error uses one JSON shape and the published code and message, and when several checks fail the published precedence decides which error is returned.

Server boundary
The server answers only same-origin writes, enforces the published size and content-type limits, and never serves source files or credentials.

Keyboard-complete dialogs
Every dialog keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside it, closes with Escape and returns focus to its opener, and every store and staff action works by keyboard with a visible focus ring.

Live regions
Cart, checkout, search, verdict, hold, upload and staff updates are announced in the named live regions with the published copy, and errors appear in alerts linked to their fields.

Reduced motion
With reduced motion requested, every published motion duration reads zero, every sequence jumps to its end state, and every interaction still works.

Editorial report look
Every screen follows the published report look: the 42% axis, the charcoal and flat-poster-colour pages, one heavy grotesk, the mosaic masthead and square corners.

Real service wiring
All state lives in PostgreSQL, search runs on Meilisearch, files go to MinIO, email goes over SMTP, and every credential is read from the environment.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and install uses npm ci.
/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package (the production tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and every bundled font with its licence.
Every shipped package and bundled font uses MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0 or OFL-1.1.
The app uses no datastore or service beyond PostgreSQL, Meilisearch, MinIO and the SMTP server.
Pages load nothing from another origin at runtime; fonts, images and scripts are served by the app.
The provided service definitions and their credentials are left unchanged.
package-lock.json is committed and the application source is TypeScript.
